title: Do Safety Policies Make Falsifiable Predictions? A Commitment-Tracking Harness

original_idea.body: A commitment-tracking harness (METR; arXiv:2512.01166): LLM extracts discrete commitments + trigger conditions from frontier policies, classifies falsifiable-vs-aspirational, records kept/broken/untestable status with citations; seed ~30 across 3-4 labs as a public accountability ledger.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: A public accountability ledger for safety commitments directly addresses governance verification; strong chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: LLM commitment extraction + classification + ledger; building a robust harness adds modest engineering.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused seeded ledger (~30 commitments) with validated extraction; harness building adds a workstream.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public documents, no lab access, policymaker-facing accountability tool; strong counterfactual value.

novelty.reasoning: METR-style commitment tracking exists; a structured falsifiability ledger is a partly-open extension.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Commitment tracking exists; structured falsifiability ledger may be open.
